scenes.changed: Milena fusses and teases and they share one joke about the debt, and the tease is what makes Inez give herself away.
beats: Have you eaten? You've looked at that Office door all shift.
Eat? With the Bureau after me? Waiting tables, I can't keep up.
I owe them too. We'll be buried with those cards half stamped.
Then bury me somewhere I can sit down.
You'd get up to look at that door. Is it so handsome?
Who's been counting? Did Okafor say something? Who else has he told?
He said nothing, you goose. You just did.
Yes, I'm seeing him. If the Office hears, it costs us both.
Not from me, they won't. Stop looking, though. You can't afford it.
Bureau loan, behind, could be cleared. Okafor, Office door, could be used.

Secret: seeing Okafor, the door guard.

scenes.changed: He answers her joke about shoes with kindness, and she believes him because he did bring the rest; one beat longer, and "Not a word that anyone knows" is cut to make room.
beats: That's the rest paid. You owe the Bureau nothing, Miss Nikolaou.
Not so loud. I've owed them since my last good shoes.
Then buy shoes first, Miss Nikolaou. We'll wait our turn.
Thank you, I mean that. Your turn. What do I owe?
A few minutes. When I telephone, call Okafor off the Office door.
Okafor. You know about us, then. What happens to him?
Easy, now. Nothing, if this goes right. And he never sees us.
You did bring the rest. I'll say it won't go by telephone.
I'm with you. I watch that square anyway. Trouble, I'll warn you.
learned: Loan paid. Inez is with us.

scenes.changed: Sky's "How's your shift, love?" gets its own beat and a fond answer, and he ends glad to be kept, so her lie hurts; one beat longer.
beats: It's time, Miss Nikolaou. Call Okafor across now. You'll do fine.
Now? With the terrace looking? Yes. All right.
Long. This door's said nothing all day. It's good to hear you.
Come across. I've something to tell you, not down a telephone.
I've this door till shift's end. For you, it can wait.
Walk, love. Don't run. Let me keep you a while.
Keep me as long as you like.
opens: Camera off? Then enter the Office.

writer.md, under How to write it: These people have lives past this talk. Warmth is a kindness, a tease, a shared joke or a fond word, and it never takes back the fear or the price.
In each scene, give one line that's said for its own sake: nobody needs it for the plot, and this person would say it anyway. Have you eaten. It stays true to the shot and the game.
Let warmth carry a fact where it can: the tease is what makes her give herself away. Warmth makes the betrayal land, so write the fondness before the lie.
Colleagues mock each other and worry about each other. Lovers are glad of each other's voices, and a little clumsy about it. The Fixer is good company, and that's why he's frightening.

writer.md, replacing.Each line does one job and leads to the: Each line follows from the last. A line may be there only because this person likes that one, once a scene.
writer.md, replacing.Everyone wants something right now, and: Everyone wants something right now, and it is never "to inform the player". Sometimes it's to make the other person laugh, or to see they've eaten.

editor.md, added to the read-aloud list: Who in this scene likes whom, and which line shows it? If none does, it's cold, and it's yours to fix.
A joke stays only if this person would make it to this person now, and it's about their life and not about the plot. A closing quip still goes.

editor.md, replacing.Does each line make the next one necessa: Does each line follow from the one before? Cut any line that only repeats or winds up to a quip. Don't cut the one line said out of fondness.
